title: Zenica residents protest unpaid one-time unemployment assistance
location: Outside the Zenica-Doboj Canton Employment Service, Zenica
organizer: Informal citizens’ group in Zenica; Medina Juhić represented participants
threshold_50_evidence: The opened report describes citizens gathering but gives no number; the 50-person threshold is unestablished.

title.summary: Zenit’s 5 January report identifies citizens protesting errors and nonpayment of the one-time 100 KM assistance.

start_date.summary: The article date and its text place the gathering on Thursday, 5 January 2023.

location.summary: The report places the protest outside the ZDK Employment Service in Zenica.

organizer.summary: The report quotes Medina Juhić as representing the informal citizens’ group.

demands.summary: The reported demand was resolution of errors/nonpayment of a government assistance payment linked to the price-increase decree.

participants_original.summary: The article says citizens gathered but gives no numerical count.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: No number or sufficiently clear qualitative description establishes at least 50 people.

end_date.summary: The article does not establish when the physical gathering ended.

protester_violence.summary: The report does not establish whether protesters used violence; silence is not coded as no.

state_response.summary: The employment-service director addressed the issue and met a representative; no evidence on arrests, beatings, dispersal, killings or shootings. No general ignore status inferred.

notes: The protest concerned nonpayment/errors in a one-time 100 KM assistance payment. The employment-service director described technical problems; a citizens’ representative met with him and reported a list-revision deadline. Do not infer that the benefit was paid.
open_questions: Verify turnout and whether the meeting/list-revision undertaking is coded as accommodation under the dataset rules.
Determine whether this and later Zenica assistance protests are distinct events in one campaign.

title: Mothers and Women of Srebrenica and Podrinje hold monthly protest in Tuzla
organizer: Mothers and Women of Srebrenica and Podrinje
threshold_50_evidence: Anadolu reports the gathering but no attendance number; threshold is unestablished.

title.summary: Anadolu names the monthly Tuzla protest and the participating women’s organizations.

start_date.summary: The article is dated 11 January 2023 and states the first annual gathering took place that day.

location.summary: The report identifies Trg Slobode in Tuzla.

organizer.summary: The report identifies Mothers and Women of Srebrenica and Podrinje.

demands.summary: The group called for enforcement of Bosnian law and sanctions for denial of genocide and insults to victims.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: No reported count or unambiguous size description establishes the 50-person threshold.

end_date.summary: The article says the gathering ended after a prayer but supplies no time or precise dissolution point.

protester_violence.summary: The report describes a peaceful protest and does not report violence; event-specific violence remains unknown.

state_response.summary: The report does not provide event-linked responses in the seven coded categories.

notes: The first reported monthly protest of 2023 asked that Bosnian laws be applied and those denying genocide or insulting victims be sanctioned. The article also quotes a call to the High Representative and domestic/international publics.
open_questions: Confirm whether the demand directed to domestic institutions meets the own-state target rule given the simultaneous appeal to the High Representative.

title: Mostar health-centre workers hold 30-minute protest and work stoppage
location: Courtyard of the Mostar Health Centre, Mostar
organizer: Mostar Health Centre employees’ union; HNK health workers and SKB Mostar colleagues expressed support
threshold_50_evidence: Both Anadolu and N1 describe the protest and stoppage but provide no crowd count.

title.summary: Anadolu and N1 separately report the 12 January Mostar health-centre protest.

start_date.summary: Both reports date the action to 12 January 2023.

location.summary: Anadolu places workers in the health-centre courtyard in Mostar.

scope.summary: Reports describe a local Mostar workplace action; additional union supporters do not establish a multi-city event.

organizer.summary: The sources identify the health-centre union and HNK health-workers union.

demands.summary: Workers sought the withheld one-time assistance payment amid inflation and cost-of-living concerns.

participants_original.summary: Neither article provides a protest attendance count.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: No attendance number or reliable 50+ description is present.

end_date.summary: The article gives a 10:00–10:30 stoppage window but does not establish when the public gathering ended.

state_response.summary: N1 quotes a union representative saying that officials had not attended or addressed the demands at this protest, while also reporting a prior government statement from 30 December. The event-specific state response is therefore left unknown; no arrests, beatings, dispersal, killings or shootings are reported.

notes: The half-hour work stoppage ran from 10:00 to 10:30 over a withheld one-time 1,080 KM assistance payment. Keep this physical January action separate from the 29 December 2022 action; no January attendance count is inferred from employee numbers.
open_questions: Verify turnout at the physical courtyard gathering; employee counts are not protest attendance.
Keep the event-specific government response unknown unless a source documents it.

title: Reported repeat Zenica unemployment-assistance protest (body unverified)
location: Zenica; exact meeting place not verified in a readable article body
organizer: Search-result copy attributes the story to Zenica.info; original author/organizer unverified
participants_original: Search-result discovery text says about 30 demonstrators; not verified against the original article.
threshold_50_evidence: Search metadata reports about thirty demonstrators, which would be below 50 if accurate; the underlying article body and exact source were not accessible, so threshold is not determined.

title.summary: Search-only headers describe a repeat Zenica protest over the one-time payment; no body has confirmed exact event wording.

start_date.summary: Discovery records connect the reported repeat protest to 12 January, but publication/event date is not body-verified.

location.summary: Search results identify Zenica; precise site is not confirmed from a read body.

organizer.summary: Discovery text points to a Zenica.info report but does not verify a formal organizer.

demands.summary: Search-only headlines associate the gathering with unpaid one-time 100 KM assistance.

participants_original.summary: Discovery text reports about thirty demonstrators; it is unverified and not treated as coded attendance.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: An unverified search-text estimate says about thirty; the “nearly 3,000” headline concerns people affected, not turnout.

protester_violence.summary: No readable body establishes violence or its absence.

state_response.summary: No readable body establishes any state response category.

notes: The Cazin and 072info search-result titles report a repeat Zenica protest and a headline about nearly 3,000 people who did not receive assistance. That 3,000 describes affected people, not participants. Search text attributes both stories to Zenica.info; no original URL was located and no copied-story body was requested.
open_questions: Identify the exact Zenica.info article URL from a reliable source, then verify date, site, turnout, organizer, demand and outcome.
Do not use the affected-population figure as protest turnout.

title: Zenica Kantonal Hospital healthcare workers protest unpaid one-time assistance
organizer: Independent Professional Union of Healthcare Employees of Zenica-Doboj Canton, hospital branch
threshold_50_evidence: Klix and a FENA dispatch report the protest but no attendance number.

title.summary: Klix and FENA report a Zenica hospital workers’ protest on 13 January.

start_date.summary: Both reports date the action to 13 January 2023.

location.summary: Both place the protest in the Kantonal Hospital Zenica grounds/courtyard.

organizer.summary: Reports identify the independent healthcare workers’ union and its hospital organization.

demands.summary: The workers sought an unpaid one-time assistance payment; amounts differ by version.

participants_original.summary: Neither account gives a count of people at the protest.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: No count or reliable qualitative description establishes 50 attendees.

state_response.summary: Management said it would make efforts toward payment; this is coded as reported engagement only, not fulfillment. No other response category is reported.

end_date.summary: The reports do not establish when the gathering ended.

protester_violence.summary: The reports do not establish protester violence.

notes: This dated January workplace action is distinct from the recurring 15-day protest series that began in October, while its campaign relationship remains open. Klix reports 1,080 KM as the allowance; the FENA version mentions a possible 800 KM amount. Both report a management undertaking to seek payment.
open_questions: Resolve whether the recurring every-15-day actions constitute a continuing episode or discrete meetings.
Verify the allowance amount against primary documentation and attendee count.

title: Zenica citizens’ protest over unpaid unemployment assistance
location: Outside the ZDK Employment Service, Zenica
participants_original: About one hundred citizens, according to the CCI quarterly report.
threshold_50_evidence: CCI’s Bosnian newsletter reports about one hundred participants; the number is approximate but clearly indicates a gathering of at least 50.

title.summary: The CCI report describes a Zenica citizens’ protest over the unpaid 100 KM assistance.

start_date.summary: The report dates the latest/final protest to 16 January 2023.

location.summary: The newsletter places the group outside the ZDK Employment Service in Zenica.

organizer.summary: The report attributes prior protests to an informal group of Zenica citizens.

demands.summary: The group sought the one-time unemployment payment established by a public price-increase relief measure.

participants_original.summary: The CCI report describes about a hundred citizens; the count is approximate, not an exact number.

participants_min.summary: “About one hundred” supports a 50+ assessment but does not establish an exact lower bound for numeric coding.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: The original-language report describes about a hundred citizens; the English edition is a translation, not independent confirmation.

end_date.summary: The newsletter does not state when the gathering ended.

protester_violence.summary: The reported passage does not establish protester violence.

state_response.summary: The cited passage does not establish any of the seven event-specific response dimensions.

notes: CCI describes this as the final/latest protest in a series over a one-time 100 KM unemployment benefit arising from the Federation government’s price-increase relief decision. S018 is an English translation of S026; they are not two independent counts. Keep the January 5 and search-only January 12 actions separate pending episode review.
open_questions: Review the approximate CCI attendance estimate and event eligibility.
Determine whether Jan 5, Jan 12 and Jan 16 were separate events within a shared campaign; keep episode_key null until reviewed.

title: Sarajevo Canton health workers hold a 30-minute warning strike
location: Primary healthcare union organizations across Sarajevo Canton; specific sites not listed
organizer: Union of Health Workers in Sarajevo Canton
threshold_50_evidence: Klix confirms a canton-wide union warning strike but gives no worker count; workplace coverage is not a participant count.

title.summary: Klix reports a health-workers’ warning strike in Sarajevo Canton.

start_date.summary: The report is dated 23 January 2023 and says the warning strike was held that day.

location.summary: The strike occurred during a break at the union’s primary healthcare organizations in Sarajevo Canton; individual sites are not named.

organizer.summary: The article identifies the Sarajevo Canton health workers’ union.

demands.summary: The union sought correction/harmonization of its collective agreement and an increase in net hourly pay.

participants_original.summary: No number of participants is reported.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: The source does not give attendance or staffing counts adequate to determine the 50-person threshold.

end_date.summary: The half-hour strike ran 10:30–11:00; the source does not establish when any associated public gathering ended.

protester_violence.summary: The report does not establish protester violence.

state_response.summary: The article reports failed negotiations before the action, not an event-specific response during/after it; all seven dimensions remain unknown.

notes: This is the health-sector half-hour warning strike held during a break on 23 January. It is separate from the eight-union general public-sector strike plan that was later moved from January to February.
open_questions: Verify attendance across sites and whether the action meets the public gathering threshold.
Do not conflate this action with the postponed eight-union warning strike.

title: RK Borac supporters protest over club premises and public case handling
location: Gathering outside the National Theatre of Republika Srpska, followed by a march to Trg Krajine, Banja Luka
threshold_50_evidence: The report says many citizens attended but provides no count; the 50-person threshold is not established.

title.summary: Banjaluka.com names the RK Borac protest and march.

start_date.summary: The report is dated 23 January 2023 and says the protest began that day.

location.summary: The article describes a gathering outside the National Theatre and a march to Trg Krajine.

organizer.summary: RK Borac director spoke at the event and the report identifies the club as the protesting organization.

demands.summary: The report presents allegations about club property and judicial/registry handling but does not state a direct demand to a domestic authority.

participants_original.summary: The phrase “many citizens” is qualitative and has no numerical count.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: “Many citizens” does not clearly establish 50 participants.

end_date.summary: The report documents a march to Trg Krajine but not its completion or dissolution.

protester_violence.summary: No protester violence is reported; unknown is retained.

state_response.summary: Police presence outside the property is reported, but no response action is described; response categories remain unknown.

notes: Speakers said the club premises were improperly transferred to a private buyer and accused public registry/court processes of irregularity. The reporting does not establish a clear demand addressed to a Bosnian state authority, and the private property dispute may be outside scope.
open_questions: Establish whether organizers made an explicit demand to a domestic state authority or challenged only a private ownership dispute.
Verify attendance threshold and physical end of the march.
